main_text.head: ORATIO ELENCTICA.
main_text.p: EXimia illa & augusta Platonis vox est, Magnifice Domine Rector, Reverendi, & Clarissimi viri, Studiosiq; lectissimi, Philosophiam minimè esse inanem inertemq; contemplationem, sed in beata regnorum gubernatione, addo ego, in Ecclesia Christi, utilem ac fructuosam. Ac prodest omninò discentibus sæpissimè artium usum, cùm in societate humana, tùm verò maximè in doctrina ea, qua salus nostra nititur, ostendere. Quem-D. Basiliusadmodum enim folia arbori sunt ornamento & usui ad fructus conservandos: Ita congruenter [illegible, ~10 letters] seu Philosophiam velut folia & corticem veritati circumducimus. Illius videlicet sapientiæ cognitionem nobis quoq; tanquam AEgyptiorum illa spolia legitimo furto licet invertere, & ad verū germanumq; usum convertere. Cùm itaque in hoc solenni conventu Academico, antequam primæ laureæ candidati ornentur, omninò, quod instituta majorum volunt, de quopiam argumento mihi verba facienda sint, quantas Dialectica & Physica Ἀκρόασις Aristotelis, quam ἀναλυτικῶς publicé tradidimus, habeat ad primæ sapientiæ sobriam explicationem opportunitates, vel unico exemplo testatius faciam, idq; eo fine, ut ad purioris Philosophiæ, inprimisq; Logicæ & Physicæ studium ac amorem divinarum rerū studiosos, qui certé omnes esse debemus, inflammem atq; exsti-

page.notes: Greek phrase after "Ita congruenter" is too faint to read reliably, so it is marked illegible. The Greek word "Ἀκρόασις" is a best reading and may be inexact. Manuscript underlining and ink marks on the page are not printed text and are left out. Faint show-through text at the top above the ornament and at the bottom is left out. Stains on the right edge are left out. The woodcut E is joined to "Eximia". No catchword is printed: the text ends with "exsti-" at the foot of the last line.
